lines.say: About 126 tokens per second, across 16 sessions, from one local setup of eight L40S cards.
This is ds4, called DwarfStar, a local inference engine for DeepSeek 4 Flash and PRO, written mostly in C.
Its goal is to run a few excellent large language models on hardware that people can actually own.
The primary target is Metal, on Macs with 96 GB or more, and it also builds for CUDA and ROCm.
You choose a build, download a model, and chat with it from a CLI, a server, or a coding agent.
That agent, ds4-agent, runs inference directly, with no separate HTTP server in between.
Sessions are saved to disk, so you can list them, resume one, or strip out the large KV payload.
Two 128 GB Macs connected with RDMA can run 4-bit DeepSeek Flash with tensor parallelism.
And ds4-eval runs embedded capability regression tests against a real model file.
To start, clone the repo, run make on Apple Silicon, and download the ds4f-q2 model.
Send this to someone who has a big Mac and wants to run DeepSeek on their own desk.
